title: Eagles’ Jalen Hurts Placed on IR with Blood Clot, Out Indefinitely – ESPN Report
body:
Philadelphia’s franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve on Monday, ending his 2026 season after doctors confirmed a blood‑clotting issue that requires immediate and ongoing treatment. The decision follows an intensive medical evaluation that began earlier in the week, during which team physicians consulted hematologists, cardiologists and vascular specialists to determine the safest course of action for the 26‑year‑old. Hurts will miss the remainder of the campaign, and the Eagles are now forced to look to their backup roster while navigating the league’s strict IR protocols that keep him sidelined for at least eight weeks.

The clot was discovered during a routine post‑game assessment after Philadelphia’s 31‑24 loss to the New York Giants on Saturday. Initial scans revealed a small thrombus in the deep veins of Hurts’ left calf, prompting an immediate ultrasound and a series of blood‑coagulation tests. While the clot itself was not life‑threatening, physicians warned that the risk of embolization—where a fragment could travel to the lungs and cause a pulmonary embolism—was significant enough to warrant a conservative approach. Hurts was placed on anticoagulant therapy and, after a multidisciplinary conference, the team opted to move him to injured reserve rather than risk a rushed return that could jeopardize his health and the Eagles’ long‑term plans.

Hurts’ abrupt exit leaves a substantial void at the helm of an offense that has been among the NFL’s most dynamic this season. Since taking over as the full‑time starter in 2023, Hurts has combined elite athleticism with a growing command of the passing game, leading the Eagles to a 7‑2 record before his injury. The backup quarterback, veteran Mitch Trubisky, who was signed earlier this year to provide depth, will now assume the starting role. Trubisky, a former Pro Bowl player with experience in both the NFC and AFC, brings a pocket‑passing style that contrasts sharply with Hurts’ dual‑threat approach. Analysts predict a shift in play‑calling, with head coach Nick Sirianni likely to lean more heavily on the ground game and short‑range passing routes to accommodate Trubisky’s strengths while minimizing the risk of further injuries to the offensive line.

The move also reshapes the Eagles’ strategic outlook for the remainder of the season and the upcoming draft. With Hurts unavailable, the team’s playoff aspirations become contingent on the depth of its roster and the ability of its defense—anchored by a formidable front seven—to keep games close. Defensive end Haason Reddick and safety C.J. Gardner‑Jones have already stepped up, but the offensive production gap may prove decisive in tight matchups against division rivals such as the Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders. Front office executives, led by GM Howie Roseman, are reportedly evaluating trade options and free‑agent signings to bolster the quarterback room, though the NFL’s trade deadline looms just days away, limiting the pool of viable candidates.

Hurts’ health issue also reignites a broader conversation about blood‑clot risks among elite athletes. While rare, clotting disorders have surfaced in recent years across multiple sports, prompting leagues to refine their medical protocols and screening processes. The Eagles’ medical staff has pledged to share findings with the NFL’s health advisory board, hoping to improve early detection and preventive measures for other players. Hurts himself released a brief statement expressing gratitude for the support he’s received and emphasizing his commitment to a full recovery before returning to the field.

Looking ahead, Philadelphia will need to rally around its new quarterback while maintaining the competitive edge that has defined its season thus far. The next few weeks will test the coaching staff’s adaptability and the resilience of the roster. If the Eagles can preserve their defensive identity and integrate Trubisky effectively, they could still contend for a postseason berth. Meanwhile, Hurts’ recovery timeline remains uncertain, but medical experts are optimistic that, with proper anticoagulation therapy and monitored rehabilitation, he could return to full strength for the 2027 campaign, where his leadership will be pivotal in the team’s long‑term aspirations.
